name.description: Optional name locally unique to the parent {@link FlowGraph}. Useful for user-facing APIs such as visualization.

inTypes.description:
key - port name
value - information about type associated with this port. This is useful for {@link FlowGraph.Edge} validation.

outTypes.description:
key - port name
value - information about type associated with this port. This is useful for {@link FlowGraph.Edge} validation.

parents.description:
ids of parent vertices in {@Workflow#parent} {@link FlowGraph}. NOTE: there can be multiple in the case
that several vertices in the parent {@link FlowGraph} were merged as part of translation to a single vertex
in the new graph.

timeout.description:
Timeout for the execution of the vertex. After timeout time has passed the vertex execution fails if not
successfully completed or failed already.

inputType.description:
Outputs will be split from a single input object or map of type specified here.
See typedoc for examples.

title:
A specialized {@link Workflow.Vertex} that represents a field or value access on an object or map, respectively.
This is often done to "split" a single {@link Workflow.Action} data output into multiple outputs.
The input of this vertex is split into one or more named outputs. The name of each output on this vertex
represents a C3 path into the input value. In other words, if the value is a {@link Map}, then the path
represents access by key, and if the value is an {@link Obj}, then the path represents field traversal.
NOTE: this type is symmetrical with {@link Workflow.Make} which combines multiple inputs.
NOTE: if the value is not an {@link Obj} or {@link Map}, then there will be an error raised.
```
                                       ----------------------                     -------------------
                                       |                    | a -------------> in | Workflow.Action |
-------------------                    |                    |                     -------------------
| Workflow.Action | out ----------> in |   Workflow.Field   |
-------------------                    |                    |                     -------------------
                                       |                    | b -------------> in | Workflow.Action |
                                       ----------------------                     -------------------
```
As an example of the field access operation, assume the {@link Workflow.Field} instance visually depicted above with
outputs `a` and `b`.
If the output of the initial action is an {@link Obj}.
```
// inputType = MyObj.myType()
type MyObj {
  a: !string
  b: !int
}
// out = MyObj(a="hello", b=42)
// a = "hello", b = 42
```
If the output of the initial action is a {@link Map}.
```
// out = {"a": "hello", "b": 42}
// a = "hello", b = 42
```
name: Workflow.Field
